To summarize, the key findings of our research, stated in one sentence that includes all relevant information, are that

(a) peer relationships serve many important functions, and (b) peer relationships are an important source of information and contacts that are used in the job search, career planning, and job performance.

(1) the functions that people receive from peer relationships in organizations are informational, future contacts and referrals; (2) these functions are more likely to be received by individuals in larger organizations or who belong to formalized network group; and (3) gender and minority status do not appear to influence peer network activity.

the functions served by peer relationships are both informational and instrumental, that the instrumental functions are more important to individuals in larger organizations, and that women and minority members are as active as majority group and male members.
